title: The neighbor
hook: Jibril kept urging kindness to the neighbor until the Prophet ﷺ thought neighbors would inherit (Bukhari)
tomorrow: Removing a stone from the road

segments.voice: Yesterday: sadaqah jariyah, the well, the tree and the knowledge that keep running. Your line was the well keeps giving. Did you teach or plant something? Day one hundred fifty-four.

Quick question: what's the name of the person who lives closest to you? Not the closest friend. The closest person. The one on the other side of your wall, or across the hall, or next door. A lot of us don't know. We know people on the other side of the world by their usernames, and we nod at the person ten feet away without ever learning their name. We send money to causes overseas, which is good, and have never knocked on the door beside ours. In Islam, charity has a starting point, and it's on the other side of your wall. Today: the neighbor.
screen: `WHO LIVES CLOSEST TO YOU?` → `A NOD, TEN FEET AWAY.` → `CHARITY HAS A STARTING POINT.`

segments.voice: Bukhari and Muslim report the Prophet ﷺ saying: Jibril kept urging me to be good to the neighbor, so much that I thought he would make the neighbor an heir. An heir. Someone with a legal share in what you leave behind, like family. That's how often the angel came back to it. The Qur'an names neighbors in Surah an-Nisa, in a list of those to be good to: parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is related to you and the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side. And Bukhari reports a warning so strong the Prophet said it three times: by Allah, he does not believe. Who? The one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm. The hadith get very practical. Sahih Muslim reports him telling the companion Abu Dharr: when you make a stew, add some extra water, and look to your neighbors. Stretch the pot. Bukhari reports him telling women not to think any gift to a neighbor too small, even a sheep's hoof. And a neighbor isn't defined by faith. Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud report that the companion Abdullah ibn Amr had a sheep slaughtered, and when he came home the first thing he asked was: have you given some to our Jewish neighbor? Because he had heard the Prophet's words about Jibril and the neighbor. Scholars have argued over how far a neighborhood stretches. But the principle is simpler than any measuring. Before the world, the house next door. Before the cause, the name.
screen: `JIBRIL KEPT URGING.` · `BY ALLAH, HE DOES NOT BELIEVE.` · `ADD WATER TO THE STEW.` · `HAVE YOU GIVEN TO OUR JEWISH NEIGHBOR?` · then, large: `START NEXT DOOR.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan to take something to a neighbor. Sit comfortably, and breathe. Picture the doors nearest yours, one by one. Which neighbors do you know? Which don't you? Pick one. Now picture something small you could bring them: extra from dinner, a few pieces of fruit, a note with your name and number, even just a hello. Not too small, remember: even a sheep's hoof. Picture knocking. Picture their face. If it makes you nervous, notice that, and breathe through it. The bell holds the time.
The neighbor. The one next door, whose rights Jibril urged so often the Prophet thought they would inherit. Today's word.
Your line: start next door. Knock on one neighbor's door this week with something small in your hand, and if you don't know their name, learn it. Day one hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims give special weight to neighbors, of any faith: sharing food, visiting, helping and avoiding any harm to them, following the hadith of Jibril and the neighbor.

fork.setup: you're making a pot of stew, just enough for your family. the Prophet ﷺ has a word for Abu Dharr about it. what is it?
options: add extra water, and look to your neighbors
fork.reveal: when you make a stew, add water and look to your neighbors (Muslim). stretch the pot.

trapdoor: what you thought: be nice to the neighbors.
what it means: the neighbor has real rights, pressed so often by Jibril the Prophet ﷺ thought they would inherit.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 6014 and Muslim 2624; 4:36 on the related and stranger neighbor; the Jewish neighbor (Tirmidhi 1943).
